nodes.label: ADR-001 Decision: Extraction Library Stack
nodes.rationale: Decided: DocumentFormat.OpenXml for OOXML (already working, no case to replace), self-compiled NPOI (Apache-2.0 source) for legacy OLE, OpenMcdf >=3.1.3 for CFB introspection. Alternatives rejected: precompiled NPOI 2.8.0+ NuGet (paid EULA), pinning pre-2.8.0 NPOI (freezes bugfixes), hand-rolling legacy parsing via OpenMcdf alone (far more work for no payoff), NPOI for OOXML too (no reason to replace working OpenXml path). Later refined by ADR-004 which found the NPOI legacy-OLE claim held only for .xls.

nodes.label: ADR-002 Decision: Profiling and Stress Testing Approach
nodes.norm_label: adr-002 decision: profiling and stress testing approach
nodes.rationale: Decided: BenchmarkDotNet as a separate benchmark project for time profiling, hand-rolled Parallel.ForEachAsync/SemaphoreSlim + Stopwatch harness (optionally + HdrHistogram.NET + dotnet-counters) for stress testing. NBomber rejected purely on its v3.0 Commercial Subscription licensing despite being the stronger engineering fit; no viable BenchmarkDotNet alternative was found worth weighing.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled Stress Harness
nodes.rationale: Chosen over NBomber as the only OSS-compliant path for sustained concurrent stress testing: Parallel.ForEachAsync/SemaphoreSlim for concurrency control plus Stopwatch for timing (~100-150 lines), optionally paired with HdrHistogram.NET for percentiles and dotnet-counters for live GC/thread-pool visibility. More implementation work than NBomber would have been, but zero licensing risk.

nodes.label: OSS-Only Library Constraint
nodes.rationale: Governing constraint driving multiple decisions: rejects NPOI's precompiled 2.8.0+ NuGet package (paid maintenance-fee EULA), rejects NBomber v3.0+ (paid Commercial Subscription requirement), and rejects commercial SDKs (Aspose, GemBox, Syncfusion, Spire, GroupDocs, LEADTOOLS) evaluated across the legacy-format and stress-testing research spikes.

nodes.label: YDK Fork Task-Dependency Bugs
nodes.rationale: Three compounding bugs in the personal ydk fork make `ydk task ready`/`ydk task start` dependency checks untrustworthy: (1) `ydk task done` never writes status:done anywhere the dependency gate reads, so manifest.yaml statuses freeze stale; (2) `ydk task create-batch` overwrites batch-mapping.json wholesale instead of merging, dropping earlier batches' slug-to-ID mappings; (3) manifest.yaml dependency lists keep referencing old placeholder slugs after ID resolution updates a task's own key but not others' references. Workaround: cross-reference `gh pr list --state merged` and hand-correct manifest.yaml, recover dropped mappings from stage-02 planning reports, and rerun a reusable remediation script (.ydk/scripts/remediate_task_status.py).

nodes.label: ADR-003 Decision: Manual Spec Review Substitution
nodes.community_name: ADR-003: Manual LLM spec review in place of `ydk spec verify`
nodes.norm_label: adr-003 decision: manual spec review substitution
nodes.rationale: YDK's Stage 01 exit criteria require `ydk spec verify` (10 Bedrock-backed reviewers) but this environment lacks AWS credentials, causing immediate NoCredentialsError. Substituted an Opus-model subagent reading each reviewer's actual rubric YAML (n01-n10) and grading real spec artifacts against those exact thresholds, iterating four grade/fix/re-grade passes until all 10 criteria cleared. Rejected alternative: skip the quality gate entirely (would violate Stage 01 exit criteria without substitute). Tradeoff: final verdict is not machine-reproducible like a Bedrock run, only a manual markdown report.

nodes.label: ADR-004 Decision: b2xtranslator for Legacy Body Text
nodes.norm_label: adr-004 decision: b2xtranslator for legacy body text
nodes.rationale: ADR-001's assumption that NPOI covers legacy doc/xls/ppt was found to hold only for .xls, since HWPFDocument (.doc) and HSLF (.ppt) live only in NPOI's unbuildable scratchpad tree. Decided: use b2xtranslator to convert .doc->.docx and .ppt->.pptx in-process, then feed through the existing OpenXml pipeline, retargeting both b2xtranslator csproj files from netcoreapp2.0 to net8.0. NPOI's HPSF/POIFS remain the answer for cross-format metadata/subfile discovery on all three legacy formats regardless of this decision. Fallback order if b2xtranslator fidelity fails: (1) port NPOI scratchpad HWPF for .doc via IllidanS4/npoi's retarget recipe, (2) LibreOffice headless subprocess conversion.

nodes.label: DocSharp (manfromarce/DocSharp)
nodes.rationale: An actively maintained MIT-licensed fork/continuation of dead-upstream b2xtranslator, multi-targeting .NET 8/9/10, with releases as recent as 2026-08-11. Not adopted as primary dependency because it is architected purely as a format converter with no common DOM/metadata API and has embedded-OLE-object extraction as an open TODO (not implemented) — self-described as a hobby project with no maintenance SLA. Bookmarked to re-check in 6-12 months.

nodes.label: IllidanS4/npoi Scratchpad Retarget Fork
nodes.rationale: A public Apache-2.0 fork that already retargeted NPOI's scratchpad HWPF/HSLF trees to SDK-style netstandard2.0 with a small identified diff, proving the port mechanically feasible. Kept as the documented fallback for .doc specifically (not adopted as primary) because HSLF (.ppt) has no working HSLFSlideShow-equivalent entry point anywhere in NPOI's C# scratchpad, requiring materially more original engineering than b2xtranslator for symmetric .doc/.ppt coverage.

nodes.label: LibreOffice Headless Subprocess Conversion
nodes.rationale: The most mature/best-fidelity option evaluated for legacy format conversion, and license-clean for subprocess use (MPL-2.0/LGPLv3, no linking). Rejected as disproportionate for now: requires bundling a 500MB+ desktop office suite, per-file process-spawn latency, and a larger sandboxing surface for a service processing untrusted input. Documented as the fallback of last resort if both b2xtranslator and a scratchpad port fail fidelity testing.

nodes.label: modeverv/dotnet-poi
nodes.rationale: Structurally the most complete single from-scratch Apache POI-equivalent port found (HSSF/HWPF/HSLF/XSSF/XWPF/XSLF), but rejected on trust/provenance grounds, not license grounds: its entire commit history spans ~48 hours, the repo is 3 months old with 1 star and no independent adoption, consistent with rapid, largely-unattended AI-agent-driven development — not an acceptable foundation for shipped-product legacy-format parsing without independent scrutiny.

nodes.label: Unicode/i18n Fidelity Requirement
nodes.rationale: Hard correctness requirement: Hebrew, Arabic, Persian, Russian, Latin, CJK text and emoji (including multi-codepoint sequences) must round-trip without mojibake or truncation, in both flat text and metadata fields. Explicitly harder on the legacy OLE read path (NPOI's Unicode fidelity there is unverified per research) than OOXML (Unicode-native via XML). Tiered contingency if a script family fails: (1) codepage-correction post-process using the OLE CodePage/\x01CompObj stream, (2) else document as a known v1 limitation with an explicit asserting test and narrow it out of acceptance criteria.
